evidence.quote: We established the OmniNA model with the LLaMA architecture [ 11 ], which is an autoregressive decoder-only transformer that adopts the self-attention mechanism.
We constructed three models with varying heads and layers, ranging from 66 M up to 1.7 B parameters ( Supplementary Fig. S2 ).
In the fine-tuning phase, the model was further trained using supervised learning on task-specific datasets.
SentencePiece [ 14 ] was employed as the subword tokenizer, resulting in a dictionary containing 32 001 tokens.
Here, the model was trained to generate text annotations (e.g. biological responses or answers to questions) given nucleotide sequences as input.
Additionally, we evaluated the fidelity of the sequence generation as the similarity between the generated sequence and the ground truth sequence.
After fine-tuning, the model can manage taxonomy and genomic element identification tasks in a QA paradigm (Fig. 1 A).
The effect score of a mutation was defined as the OmniNA-1.7B estimated LL between mutated and wild-type nucleotide sequences (Fig. 5 A).

We further benchmarked OmniNA-1.7B against current state-of-the-art nucleotide sequence foundation models, including DNABERT2 [ 20 ], Nucleotide Transformer-v2 [ 21 ], and Hyena-DNA [ 22 ], in terms of feature representation performance.
OmniNA1.7B outperforms all other models across 11 feature representation tasks

representation_comparisons.result_summary: OmniNA-1.7B outperformed DNABERT2, Nucleotide Transformer-v2, and Hyena-DNA across 11 feature representation tasks.

evidence.quote: By jointly modeling both sequences and their associated annotations, our approach seeks to more fully capture the compositional grammar and semantic structure underlying genomic information, enabling robust generalization and interpretability across tasks.

representation_rationale.summary: Joint sequence-and-annotation modeling is intended to capture nucleotide grammar and annotation semantics.

evidence.quote: This dual modality allows for complementary information exchange between sequences and annotations, enabling the model to develop a more holistic understanding and representation of biological data.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors motivate the dual modality through complementary information exchange and a holistic biological representation.

evidence.quote: Compared with sequence-only foundation models, such as DNABERT2 [ 20 ], Nucleotide Transformer-v2 [ 21 ], and Hyena-DNA [ 22 ], OmniNA-1.7B demonstrates superior feature representation capabilities, particularly in tasks requiring fine-grained sequence discrimination.

representation_rationale.summary: The authors contrast their sequence-plus-annotation design with sequence-only foundation models.

evidence.quote: Second, finetuning performance can be influenced by the quality and completeness of annotations used during pretraining. Although OmniNA leverages annotations only as weak cues and performs sequence-only inference, noisy labels can still affect learned representations.

representation_rationale.summary: Annotation quality and completeness can affect learned representations and fine-tuning performance.

evidence.quote: Lastly, OmniNA is currently limited to processing sequences of ∼ 3000 base pairs, which may restrict its ability to capture long-range regulatory interactions such as distal enhancer -promoter coordination and 3D chromatin effects.

representation_rationale.summary: The sequence-length limit restricts modeling of long-range regulatory interactions.
